title: Rapid transfer brief — midday inference ops
content:
Context:
Quick handover notes for the midday relay — keep this compact. Personal checklist for the next 4–6h window. Not a canonical runbook, just what I'd want to know if I'm stepping in cold.

CURRENT STATE (as of 2025-03-10 11:45PT):
- No active SevX incidents.
- Elevated generation latency on hosted-api-prod-us-west for short bursts (p95 ~ 420ms -> 880ms intermittently).
- Dedicated cluster rt-pool-3 shows 12% lower throughput due to two eviction restarts yesterday (OOM-kill suspected).

Quick triage steps (first 10m):
1) Check core metrics dashboard (Console -> Models -> prod -> latency heatmap). Look for pattern by model/version.
2) Inspect recent deploys: `gitlab: /infra/deploys` and `kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` for restarts.
3) Confirm autoscaler activity: `kubectl describe hpa inference-api -n inference` and check tsdb for scale-up events around spike times.
4) If p95 > 500ms and errors/429s present, flip route to canary fallback model (route: /models/compatible/fallback-small) for affected customer-tier (see routing policy doc in Confluence).

Useful commands (copy to shell):
- k debug: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference | grep prod`
- tail logs for a bad pod: `kubectl -n inference logs pod/<name> -c inference-runtime --since=30m`
- check eviction reasons: `kubectl -n inference describe pod <name> | grep -i OOM`
- check GPU memory pressure: `nvidia-smi` on node (ssh via bastion)

Temporary mitigations I've used before:
- Remove large batch-size flags for the short burst window by updating the route config (console quick edit).
- Enable per-route KV cache warmup for top 3 models (helps short-seq latency).
- For obvious OOM, cordon node and evict the pod set then scale up pool by +1 temporarily.

Escalation/contact list:
- Primary SRE: Samir Gupta (slack @samir, phone x4-220)
- Runtime lead: Lena Cho (slack @lena)
- On-call eng (backend): insp-rotation channel (slack #oncall-eng)
- Pager: if incident is Sev2+, page mobile and then #all-hands if >30m degraded.

Notes to self / items to follow up (post-shift):
- Open ticket RW-2241 to investigate repeated OOMs in rt-pool-3 (assigned to Samir). Add heap snapshots and eviction logs.
- Revisit quantization fallback rules: sometimes fallback model causes output drift — add small eval to ensure quality doesn't regress.
- Add a quick link in Console to the runbook section for the fallback route (current path buried in Confluence).

Unresolved questions / heuristics I'm testing:
- Is the latency spike correlating with a specific seq_len distribution? (I suspect a small set of customers sending long context in bursts)
- Are autoscaler thresholds tuned for short-lived bursts vs sustained traffic? Might need a burst policy.

Housekeeping / quick TODOs for incoming shift:
- If you see >3 pods with restarts in 1h, escalate directly to Samir.
- If error rate above 1% for any model, route to fallback and notify product owner.
- Add a comment in RW-2241 when you do any manual node cordon/uncordon.

Quick references (one-liners):
- Serving logs & traces: Console -> Observability -> Traces (filter model=prod)
- Deployment history: GitLab / infra-deploys -> tags
- Incident page template: Confluence -> Incident Playbook -> create from template

Final: I'm leaving the console links pinned in my browser and a Slack thread (slack:#infra-oncall) with the last 4 events. If you take over, say hi to Samir and drop a quick summary in the thread so we don't duplicate mitigations.

— E.P.
